title: Air India serves Navratri feast at 35,000 feet: sabudana vada, makhana kheer
excerpt: A fasting-friendly menu — sabudana khichdi, vratwala paneer, samak jeera rice and more — runs October 10–20 on select flights from Delhi, Mumbai and Ahmedabad, with a Navratri food cart at the Maharaja Lounge.
body:
• Air India has rolled out a Navratri-special menu for October 10–20, 2026, on select flights from Delhi, Mumbai and Ahmedabad, plus festive menus at its Delhi and Mumbai lounges.
  • Onboard highlights: Sabudana Khichdi, Sabudana Wada, Vratwala Shahi Paneer, Samak Jeera Rice, Singhade ki Poori and Sabudana Fruit Kheer — all made with shuddh ghee and sendha namak.
  • The Maharaja Lounge in Delhi adds a Navratri food cart with Farali Misal, Farali Kachori, Shakarkandi ki Tikki, Rajgira specialties and Makhana Kheer on request.
  • Sharad Navratri 2026 runs October 11–19, with Dussehra on October 20 — the airline's ten-day menu window covers the entire festival.

Air India is taking Navratri to 35,000 feet. The airline has introduced a specially curated fasting-friendly menu for the festival, served on select flights operating from Delhi, Mumbai and Ahmedabad during the ten days of festivities from October 10 to 20, 2026, according to a report by BOTT India.

Context & Background

Navratri's vrat (fast) traditions come with strict food rules: no onion, garlic, grains, or regular table salt. For airlines, that makes festival menus a logistical challenge — every dish must respect the fast while still working at altitude. Air India's answer is a full-course vrat menu prepared with shuddh ghee and sendha namak (rock salt), the two cornerstones of fasting-friendly cooking.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=uw6pQkJ0zQA

"Context & Background Navratri's vrat (fast) traditions come with strict food rules: no onion, garlic, grains, or regular table salt."

Sharad Navratri 2026 runs from October 11 to October 19, with Dussehra falling on October 20 — so the airline's October 10–20 window covers the entire festival, as detailed in this Navratri 2026 dining guide.

Impact & Analysis

The onboard menu is structured across the day's services. Breakfast brings Sabudana Khichdi with crispy potato salli, Vratwale Shahi Aloo and Singhade ki Poori, served with fresh fruit and plain dahi. The refreshment service offers Sabudana Wada, Garam Aloo Chaat prepared with sendha namak and mint chutney, Vratwala Paneer Tikka enriched with curd, cashew and aromatic spices, alongside Sabudana Fruit Kheer and fresh fruit. For lunch and dinner, passengers get Vratwala Shahi Paneer, Vratwali Kaddu Ki Subzi, Samak Jeera Rice and Singhade ki Poori, again with fruit, dahi and Sabudana Fruit Kheer.

The celebration extends to the ground. Air India is turning its lounges in Delhi and Mumbai into festive culinary stops: the flagship Maharaja Lounge in Delhi serves Sabudana Khichdi, Farali Misal, Farali Kachori, Shakarkandi ki Tikki, Sabudana Vada, Rajgira specialties and Makhana Kheer on request, with a bespoke Navratri food cart adding ceremony to the lounge experience.

This is part of a pattern: the Air India group has been leaning into festival catering — sister carrier Air India Express has served Sattvik Navratri meals and Onam Sadya on its international flights — as Indian carriers compete on cultural hospitality, not just price and punctuality.

Diaspora Angle

For NRIs flying home during the festive season, the vrat question is a real one: long-haul flights with standard meal service can force fasting passengers to skip meals entirely. A fasting-compliant menu on the Delhi, Mumbai and Ahmedabad sectors means devotees observing Navratri don't have to choose between the fast and eating on the journey. Travellers planning to fly during October 11–20 can check festive meal availability and request special meals in advance through airindia.com's Manage My Booking before their flight.

What's Next

The menu runs through October 20, 2026, covering Dussehra. With Diwali following in early November, expect the festive-catering playbook to return — and watch whether other Indian carriers answer with their own festival menus as the peak travel season unfolds.

steps: Heat the ghee in a pan and sauté the makhana until golden.
In a separate pan, heat the milk and let it simmer for 8–10 minutes.
Add the sautéed makhana (lotus seeds) and cook for a couple more minutes, then stir in the condensed milk.
Add sugar to taste and a pinch of cardamom powder; garnish with chopped pistachios and serve.
Recipe: Executive Chef Avinash Kumar, Novotel Imagica Khopoli, via Indulge Express.
